en: I wish to know the truth about renunciation, mighty-armed, and about relinquishment as distinct from it, Hrishikesha, slayer of Keshi.
speaker: Arjuna said

sa: काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः।
tr: kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ
en: The wise understand renunciation as giving up actions driven by desire; the discerning call giving up the fruits of all actions relinquishment.
speaker: Krishna said

en: Some thinkers say all action should be given up as flawed; others say acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity should not be given up.

sa: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम।
tr: niścayaṃ śrṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama
en: Hear my conclusion about relinquishment, best of the Bharatas; for relinquishment, tiger among men, is declared to be of three kinds.
Acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity should not be given up but should be performed; sacrifice, giving and austerity purify even the wise.

sa: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च।
tr: etānyapi tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca
en: But even these actions should be done giving up attachment and the fruits, Partha. That is my settled and highest view.
Renouncing a duty that is one's own is not right; giving it up out of delusion is declared to be of dullness.

sa: स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥
tr: sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet
en: Whoever gives up an action because it is painful, out of fear of bodily hardship, makes a relinquishment of passion and does not gain its fruit.

sa: सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥
tr: saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ
en: When a duty is performed simply because it ought to be done, Arjuna, giving up attachment and its fruit, that relinquishment is of goodness.
The relinquisher filled with goodness, wise, with doubts cut away, does not hate unpleasant work nor cling to pleasant work.

sa: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः।
tr: na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ
en: It is not possible for an embodied being to give up actions entirely; but one who gives up the fruits of action is called a true relinquisher.

sa: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम्।
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥
tr: aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam
bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit
en: The fruit of action, unwanted, wanted and mixed, comes after death to those who have not relinquished; but never to those who have renounced.
Learn from me, mighty-armed, these five causes for the accomplishment of every action, as declared in the Sankhya teaching:

sa: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्।
tr: adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham
en: the body, the doer, the various instruments, the many kinds of effort, and fifth, providence.

sa: न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥
tr: nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ
en: Whatever action a person undertakes with body, speech or mind, right or wrong, these five are its causes.

sa: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः।
tr: tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ
en: That being so, whoever, through untrained understanding, sees the Self alone as the doer, that dull-minded person does not see.

sa: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते।
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥
tr: yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate
hatvāpi sa imā~llokānna hanti na nibadhyate
en: One who is free from the notion "I am the doer" and whose understanding is not tainted, even if they slay these people, does not slay and is not bound.
Knowledge, the known and the knower are the threefold impulse to action; the instrument, the action and the doer are the threefold basis of action.

sa: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः।
tr: jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ
en: Knowledge, action and the doer are of three kinds according to the qualities, as taught in the science of the qualities. Hear about these too.
That knowledge by which one sees the one imperishable being in all beings, undivided in the divided, know to be of goodness.

sa: वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
tr: vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi rājasam
en: But knowledge that sees in all beings many separate entities of different kinds, know that knowledge to be of passion.
And knowledge that clings to one single thing as if it were the whole, without reason, without grasp of the truth, and narrow, is said to be of dullness.
Action that is required, done without attachment, without love or hate, by one who does not want its fruit, is said to be of goodness.

sa: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः।
tr: yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥ
en: Action done with great strain by one who craves desires or is driven by ego is said to be of passion.
Action undertaken out of delusion, without regard for consequences, loss, harm to others or one's own ability, is said to be of dullness.
A doer free from attachment, not boastful, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged in success and failure, is said to be of goodness.
A doer who is passionate, eager for the fruits of action, greedy, violent, impure, and swept by joy and sorrow is said to be of passion.

sa: विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
tr: viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate
en: A doer who is undisciplined, coarse, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating is said to be of dullness.
Now hear, Dhananjaya, the threefold division of understanding and of firmness according to the qualities, told fully and one by one.

sa: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये।
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
tr: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye
bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
en: The understanding that knows when to act and when to refrain, what is to be done and what not, what to fear and what not, what binds and what frees, Partha, is of goodness.

sa: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च।
tr: yayā dharmamadharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryameva ca
en: The understanding by which one wrongly grasps dharma and adharma, what is to be done and what not, Partha, is of passion.
The understanding which, wrapped in darkness, takes adharma for dharma and sees all things upside down, Partha, is of dullness.
The firmness by which one holds the workings of mind, breath and senses through unwavering yoga, Partha, is of goodness.

sa: प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
tr: prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
en: But the firmness by which one holds to duty, pleasure and wealth, craving their fruits through attachment, Arjuna, is of passion.

sa: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च।
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
tr: yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madameva ca
na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
en: The firmness by which a foolish person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, depression and arrogance, Partha, is of dullness.

sa: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ।
tr: sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śrṛṇu me bharatarṣabha
en: Now hear from me the three kinds of happiness, best of the Bharatas: that in which one delights through practice, and in which sorrow comes to an end,
which is like poison at first but like nectar in the end: that happiness is said to be of goodness, born of the clarity of one's own understanding.
Happiness that comes from the contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first and like poison in the end, is said to be of passion.
Happiness that deludes the self at the beginning and at the end, arising from sleep, laziness and carelessness, is said to be of dullness.

sa: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः।
tr: na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ
en: There is no being on earth, or among the gods in heaven, who is free from these three qualities born of nature.
The duties of brahmins, kshatriyas, vaishyas and shudras, scorcher of foes, are divided according to the qualities born of their own nature.
Calm, self-control, austerity, purity, patience, uprightness, knowledge, realisation and faith are the duties of the brahmin, born of their nature.
Heroism, vigour, steadiness, skill, not fleeing from battle, generosity and leadership are the duties of the kshatriya, born of their nature.
Farming, tending cattle and trade are the duties of the vaishya, born of their nature; work that serves others is the duty of the shudra, born of their nature.

sa: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः।
tr: sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ
en: Devoted to their own work, each person attains perfection. Hear how, devoted to their own work, one finds perfection.
By worshipping, through one's own work, the One from whom all beings come and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.
Better your own dharma, even imperfectly done, than another's done well. Doing the work set by one's own nature, one incurs no sin.

sa: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्।
tr: sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet
en: One should not give up the work one is born to, son of Kunti, even if it has flaws; for every undertaking is covered by flaws, as fire is by smoke.
With understanding unattached everywhere, self-controlled, free from craving, one reaches through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.

sa: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे।
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥
tr: siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me
samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā
en: Hear from me briefly, son of Kunti, how one who has reached perfection reaches Brahman, the highest state of knowledge.

sa: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च।
tr: buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyā''tmānaṃ niyamya ca
en: Endowed with a pure understanding, controlling oneself with firmness, turning away from sound and the other objects of sense, letting go of attraction and aversion,
living in solitude, eating lightly, controlling speech, body and mind, always devoted to meditation and yoga, taking refuge in dispassion,

sa: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम्।
tr: ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham
en: having given up ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, free from "mine" and at peace, one is fit to become Brahman.

sa: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥
tr: brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām
en: Become one with Brahman, serene, one neither grieves nor craves; the same to all beings, one attains supreme devotion to me.

sa: ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥
tr: tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram
en: By devotion one comes to know me truly, what and who I am; then, knowing me in truth, one enters into me at once.
Though always doing all actions, taking refuge in me, by my grace one reaches the eternal, imperishable abode.
Inwardly offering all actions to me, making me your highest goal, relying on the yoga of understanding, keep your mind always on me.
With your mind on me, by my grace you will cross every obstacle; but if out of ego you do not listen, you will be lost.
If, relying on ego, you think "I will not fight," your resolve is in vain; your own nature will compel you.
Bound by your own work, born of your nature, son of Kunti, what you do not wish to do out of delusion you will do even against your will.
The Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, Arjuna, causing all beings to turn by his power, as if mounted on a machine.
Take refuge in him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By his grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
So I have given you this knowledge, more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.

sa: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
tr: sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śrṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ
iṣṭo'si me dṛḍhamiti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam
en: Hear again my supreme word, the most secret of all. You are dearly loved by me, so I will tell you what is good for you.

sa: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु।
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥
tr: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru
māmevaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo'si me
en: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, offer to me, bow to me. You will come to me; I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.

sa: अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
tr: ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
en: Letting go of all dharmas, take refuge in me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.

sa: न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥
tr: na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo'bhyasūyati
en: This should never be told to one who lacks austerity or devotion, or who does not wish to listen, or who speaks ill of me.
Whoever teaches this supreme secret to my devotees, showing the highest devotion to me, will come to me without doubt.

sa: भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥
tr: bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi
en: There is no one among humans who does dearer service to me than they, nor will there be anyone on earth dearer to me.

sa: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः।
tr: adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ
en: And whoever studies this sacred dialogue of ours, by them I shall be worshipped with the sacrifice of knowledge; that is my view.
And whoever simply hears it with faith and without finding fault, they too, freed, will reach the happy worlds of the righteous.
Have you heard this with an undistracted mind, Partha? Has your delusion born of ignorance been destroyed, Dhananjaya?
My delusion is destroyed, and I have regained my memory by your grace, Achyuta. I stand firm, my doubts gone. I will do as you say.
speaker: Arjuna said

en: So I heard this wondrous dialogue between Vasudeva and the great-souled Partha, and it makes my hair stand on end.
speaker: Sanjaya said

en: By the grace of Vyasa I heard this supreme, secret yoga directly from Krishna, the lord of yoga himself, as he spoke it.
O king, as I remember again and again this wondrous and holy dialogue between Keshava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

sa: विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥
tr: vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
en: And as I remember again and again that most wondrous form of Hari, great is my amazement, O king, and I rejoice again and again.

sa: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः।
tr: yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ
en: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and wherever there is Partha, the archer, there will be fortune, victory, prosperity and sound policy. That is my conviction.
